entries.en: I have walked the whole path here,
and my longing turns over and over.
entries.note: The libretto has 情思; this performance sings 思情. The sense is the same.

entries.en: Everything in the garden is as it was.
While it is quiet and no one is near,
now is the time to look for my dream.
Is that spot over there beside the rockery?
entries.note: 湖山石 is an ornamental garden rock of the kind taken from lake beds.

entries.en: And this, it seems, is the edge of the Peony Pavilion.
Along the carved railing the peony shoots are just showing,
entries.note: 芍药 is the herbaceous peony, a different plant from the tree peony (牡丹) of the pavilion's name.

entries.en: the willows hang down thread by thread,
and the elm seeds lie like tiny coins.
entries.note: Elm seed pods (榆荚) are called elm money for their round, coin-like shape. The performance sings 英 where the libretto has 荚.

entries.key: 啊线儿春甚金钱啊吊转#1
entries.zh: 啊线儿春甚金钱啊吊转
entries.en: Ah, could these threads string those coins and win spring back?
entries.note: A play on the willow threads and elm coins of the two lines before: coins were strung on a cord. The two 啊 are padding syllables added in performance.

entries.en: Yesterday, in my dream,
that scholar brought me a willow branch as a gift
and asked me to write a poem on it.
And when he pressed me to be his lover...
entries.note: 奴 is a humble feminine word for I; the libretto has 我.

entries.en: oh, that is a long story to tell!
Whose handsome young man was it who came so near,
who dared to coax a girl from her chamber into the garden?
entries.note: 沁园 was the name of a Han princess's garden; here it simply means a fine garden.

entries.en: When I come to what happened next, I blush.
He narrowed his eyes and gazed at me,
so patient with me, oh heaven!
entries.note: 奈烦 is an old spelling of 耐烦, patient.

entries.en: and I opened my lips,
meaning to answer him.
We were not lovers in a former life,
nor had we ever so much as glimpsed each other.
I would have thought he might appear in a life to come,
yet suddenly, in this life, I met him in a dream.
Every inch a scholar,
entries.note: This aria plays on the word 生 (life, born, scholar) in almost every line; the wordplay does not carry into English.

entries.en: he simply took me in his arms and laid me down.
I have searched and searched,
and it is all gone.
The Peony Pavilion,
the peony railing:
how did they become so bleak and forlorn,
with no trace of anyone?
How it grieves me!
In a place as desolate as this,
entries.note: The libretto begins 是这等; the performance sings 似这等.

entries.en: with hardly a pavilion or terrace close by,

entries.key: 敢是咱眯睎色眼寻难见#1
entries.zh: 敢是咱眯睎色眼寻难见
entries.en: can it be my own bleary eyes that fail to find it?
Here it is broad daylight under a clear sky,
entries.note: The libretto has 明放着, plainly here; the first word is not sung in this performance.

entries.en: yet I cannot catch hold of what my dreaming soul saw.
For an instant it is as if it lived again;
I turn about on the spot, hoping to make it linger.
It was here, right here, that my gold bracelet was pressed flat.
entries.note: She has found the place where the two lay together in the dream.

entries.en: Scholar!
Scholar!
Ah!
Here, where no one comes,
I suddenly see a great plum tree.
entries.note: 梅 (méi) is the Chinese flowering plum. It is also the last word of her dream lover's name, Liu Mengmei.

entries.en: Look at its plums, cluster on cluster. How lovely!
entries.note: The libretto has 磊落; the performance says 累累, in heavy clusters.

entries.en: If I, Liniang, could be buried here when I die,
how fortunate that would be!
All at once my heart is bound fast,
here beside the plum tree.

entries.key: 似这等花花草草由人恋#1
entries.zh: 似这等花花草草由人恋
entries.en: If flowers and grasses like these were ours to love as we chose,
if living and dying went as we wished,
then, bitter as the sorrow is, no one would complain.
entries.note: The libretto line ends with 怨, complain. That word is not sung in this performance, but the translation keeps the full sense.

entries.en: I will gather up this one fragrant soul
and, through the dark rains of plum season,
entries.note: 梅天 is the rainy season of early summer, when the plums ripen.

entries.en: ah, my love,
keep watch at the plum tree's roots until we meet.
A fair lady gathers spring greens in the courtyard;
entries.note: The maid Chunxiang enters with a couplet. 拾翠, gathering green things, is a set phrase for a lady's spring outing.

entries.en: her maid adds incense in the still noon court.
I wonder where my young mistress has gone.
Oh!
Look, she has walked herself tired
and dozed off beside the plum tree.
Miss!
Miss!
Chunxiang.
Miss.
I,
Liniang...
Even the blossoms by my upstairs room, for certain,
will shine only on one who sleeps alone.
